description: Participants answer a fictional regional tourism board's questions by exploring its data, starting every analysis from written questions. They profile tables, examine distributions, relationships and change over time, build charts with a grammar of graphics and scales that do not mislead, and test by resampling whether a pattern could be chance. They repair misleading charts and write findings that state what is and is not shown, in a notebook that reruns from raw data.
audience: Practitioners. Graduates and early-career analysts who have completed the FN courses or passed the placement test, and analysts moving into data science.
prerequisites: FN-101 Python for Data and AI Work
Makes a basic chart in any plotting library

outcomes.text: Distinguish exploratory from confirmatory analysis and explain why a pattern found by exploring needs a fresh test, given five findings from a past board report
outcomes.evidence: each finding marked exploratory or confirmed, with the check it would need

outcomes.text: Prepare an analysis plan listing questions, units of observation, variables and the comparison that answers each, given the director's brief and the data dictionary
outcomes.evidence: a one-page plan checked against a checklist before any chart is drawn

outcomes.text: Analyse distributions, relationships and change over time with summaries and charts suited to each variable type, given three years of visitor, occupancy and survey tables
outcomes.evidence: a chart, a summary statistic and a two-sentence reading per question

outcomes.text: Use a grammar of graphics to map variables to position, colour and facets with honest scales, baselines and labels, given six misleading charts from earlier reports
outcomes.evidence: six repaired charts, each with the fault and the fix named

outcomes.text: Test whether an apparent difference or correlation could arise by chance, using permutation or bootstrap resampling, given three patterns the board wants to announce
outcomes.evidence: each pattern's resampling result and a decision to report, qualify or drop it

outcomes.text: Deliver a reproducible exploratory report that states findings, uncertainty, open questions and limits for a non-specialist reader, given an unseen dataset and a named audience
outcomes.evidence: a rendered report and notebook that rerun from raw data, defended live
